newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central banker sees 97 GDP at 6.0 pct-paper.
newsitem.headline: Thai central banker sees 97 GDP at 6.0 pct-paper.

text.p: Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond said the country's gross domestic product (GDP) should grow about six percent in 1997, local newspapers reported on Monday.

Krungthep Thurakit newspaper quoted Rergnchai as saying he would continue a policy focusing on maintaining economic stability instead of growth which would trim GDP growth to about six percent this year against 7.1 originally projected by the Bank of Thailand.
The central bank had since revised its projection down to 6.8 percent for the year.
A central bank official told Reuters on Monday that Rerngchai made the comments as an early indication of the bank's expected downward revision of macroeconomic figures.
The government is due to release a revised list of economic indicators this week.
A sharp slowdown of Thailand's once robust economy has worried investors and been one of the reasons behind the bourse's fall to 6-1/3 year lows in the past week.
For the past decade the economy grew by an average of about nine percent a year and six percent growth is seen by local investors as a sharp slowdown.
The government has blamed weak exports for the slowdown.
